items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: I remember the first job I played with Lee Collin. Lee Collin was the first guy I worked with here.

ctx.x: What happened after you, in music after that?

Well what happened after music after, then I came to New Orleans and I joined the Bud Roussel band. I remember the first job I played with Lee Collin. Lee Collin was the first guy I worked with here. Bud Roussel, played a place back at the, it was a station up on Ramport Street, and I was a place back there used to be called the Function. I remember one Saturday night I got a job playing with Bud Roussel and Lee Collin, who happened to be playing trumpet in that band. Did you work regularly with him? Yeah, I…
Who was in Bud Roussel's band? Do you remember other than Lee?

items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: I remember the first job I played with Lee Collin. Lee Collin was the first guy I worked with here.

ctx.x: And who was in Jack Carey's band? Different fellas or was it pretty scary or what?

I know Black Happy was the drummer. Jack Carey played trombone. Who else played? I don't know who was playing trumpet. Lee, yeah, Lee Collin played with him for a while. I can't think of the bass player. I used to work also with Duke and Forstay. You ever heard of Trombone Play by the name of Forstay?

And Duke and his two brothers? The brother played trumpet? Yeah. He used to work with Joe Avery and Wilbur Tilma when I first came in 1945. He died. I have a private recording of the mother's play, you know, in Mayden. For me, just for something to remember him by when I was a young lady. He played nice.
